title: Call-safety patterns: cross-service retry/timeout/backoff, idempotency keys, and hedged requests for multi-region failover
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem statement: Services and SDKs across Redwood have inconsistent retry/timeout/backoff behaviors. This leads to cascading tail-latency, duplicate side-effects (when idempotency is not enforced), and unclear behavior during multi-region failover. We need a single, opinionated call-safety contract that: (1) maps to SLOs and service-level error budgets, (2) provides clear SDK defaults and opt-outs, (3) standardizes idempotency key semantics and format, (4) defines hedged request guidelines, and (5) integrates with circuit breakers and load-shedding policies for multi-region routing.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical RetryPolicy spec exists and is checked into the runtime repo (docs + JSON schema)
SDKs (Go, Python, TypeScript) implement the RetryPolicy with identical defaults and expose opt-outs
Idempotency header X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key defined with format and TTL; servers reject/ack duplicates with documented responses
Hedged request policy defined: when hedging is allowed, max hedged attempts = 2, hedging delay = adaptive based on p99 latency
Circuit breaker thresholds per region and default load-shedding response payload implemented in runtime
Runbook for outage scenarios (region down, network partitions) published and linked from Console incident page
work_items: Draft RetryPolicy JSON schema and publish in docs - (Maya) - 2d
Define X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key format + server storage TTL (24h default) - (Luis) - 1d
Implement SDK header auto-generation + opt-out flag - (SDK team) - 3d
Runtime changes: accept idempotency header, store dedupe metadata, expose metric 'idempotency_dedup_hits' - (Runtime) - 4d
Hedging: add hedged request shim in request router, integrate with batching logic - (Routing) - 5d
Circuit breaker: wire region-level failure counts into smart routing decisions - (SRE) - 3d
Write regression tests + chaos scenarios for multi-region failover - (QE) - 3d
Update Console docs and rollout notes - (Docs) - 2d
decisions: Use exponential backoff with full jitter as default: base 50ms, cap 3s, factor 2.0
Client-side retry budget: max 3 attempts for idempotent-safe operations, 1 attempt for non-idempotent unless idempotency key present
Idempotency key format: <service-prefix>|<uuid-v4>|<iso8601-ts-hash> and propagated over header X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key
Hedging allowed only for read-like, latency-sensitive endpoints (generation streaming, model inference). Max 2 concurrent attempts, hedging delay is dynamic computed from moving-window p95 latency
Circuit breaker tripping: error-rate > 10% over 1m AND p99 latency degraded by > 2x triggers region fallback
Load-shedding responds with structured error 429 + 'retry_after' + 'fallback_recommendation' when capacity exceeded
Server-side dedup semantics: accept-first-write semantics with idempotency metadata stored for TTL; clients receive 200/202 for duplicate if original succeeded
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive client retries reduce user-visible failure but can increase pressure on degraded region and amplify outage. To mitigate we bind retry behaviour to SLO-aligned retry budget and runtime-side circuit breakers.
Hedging increases headroom for transient tail latency but can double upstream load; limited hedging + adaptive delay reduces worst-case amplification.
Idempotency TTL must balance storage cost vs duplicate suppression window. Default 24h chosen based on typical user retries and observed duplicate side-effect window.
We considered using vector timestamps for idempotency but rejected for complexity; opted for simple client-supplied keys plus server dedupe state.

Security: idempotency keys are not sensitive but should be logged with caution. We will redact in high-volume telemetry and support KMS-based signing if product requires proof of origin. Security review required before GA.
